gm_decisions.ruling_narrative: Canada confirms carve-outs must be in binding text, not side memo; trilateral structure solidifies.

_reactions.ustr: Alright, here's what's blocking us: on that 75% RVC phase-in, we need explicit carve-out language for inputs where North American supply literally doesn't exist—semiconductors, rare earths, specialty chemicals. Day-one enforcement on impossible inputs means auto moves those lines to Asia before we even sign. So: do we lock carve-out categories in the text with a year-three trilateral review to phase them in, or do we leave it vague and watch supply chains relocate? I need that answer today.
_reactions.mexico_neg: Alright—carve-outs in the text, year-three review, we're solid on that. But here's what closes this: labor audits run through Mexican labor ministry with U.S. and Canadian observers embedded—that language goes *into* the same trilateral text as the auto carve-outs, not negotiated later. One agreement, one ratification, Congress sees a package. Canada, USTR—are we writing that enforcement structure into the trilateral right now, or does it float separately and kill the deal on the Hill?
_reactions.us_congress: Canada, USTR's not bluffing—if you don't commit to 75% RVC and the labor floor now, Congress ratifies a U.S.-Mexico deal and kills the whole trilateral on the Hill. My folks won't vote for a deal that looks like we abandoned our largest trading partner. So: yes or no on the full package—RVC, wage floor, audits, carve-outs, year-three review—all in the trilateral text?
_reactions.auto_industry: Okay, carve-outs locked in the text—that works. But at year three, when you're reviewing those inputs, what's the actual trigger? Do we automatically hit 75% RVC on semiconductors if North American capacity still doesn't exist, or does the review open the carve-out categories back up for negotiation?
_reactions.labor_union: USTR, hold on — at year three, when you're reviewing semiconductors and rare earths, what actually happens? Do those carve-outs auto-renew if North American supply still doesn't exist, or does the review blow them back open for renegotiation? Because if it's the latter, my members start moving those lines to Asia *right now* — they're not restructuring supply chains for three years if the carve-out expires.
_reactions.dairy_ag: Hold on—before we lock carve-outs and labor audits into the text, dairy phased access has to go in *the same agreement*, same section, same ratification vote. Three-year phase-in for dairy market access: Canada commits to specific tariff reductions on U.S. dairy products, quarterly verification, automatic triggers if Canada misses targets. Congress won't ratify autos-only—I'm telling you that flat. Is dairy in the trilateral text now, or do we walk?
_reactions.supply_chain_mfr: USTR, one thing before dairy locks in: at year three, do semiconductors and rare earths auto-renew their carve-outs if North American capacity still doesn't exist, or does the review reopen negotiation? Because if it's renegotiation, my supply chains start moving those lines offshore *now*—they're not betting three years on a carve-out that expires.
